scores.accuracy_concern: The McCurry 2007 'two-thirds of dementia carers' figure is a background estimate in the review abstract, not a finding; the Pesonen nocturia-falls link (pooled RR 1.20) is observational and very low certainty as a cause; NICE NG27 was not openable, so the discharge-guidance claim needs a published copy.
scores.sharpen: Rest the post on one checkable fact (night-time urination is common and linked with falls) and make the checklist card the post, with one named question for the discharge meeting.

scores.accuracy_concern: The donepezil SPC advises evening dosing. Moving the dose to the morning when sleep is disturbed is common practice but needs a citable source. The BNF and SPCs were not openable, so the diuretic, steroid and donepezil timing claims need published sources. Parkinson's overnight wearing-off advice must match the NG71 wording.
scores.sharpen: Lead with the annotated drug chart and keep only the two or three timing fixes with citable sources; say that moving a dose is a plan for tomorrow night, while tonight's call is for pain, bladder and noise.

scores.accuracy_concern: EMPOWER: 27% versus 5% had discontinued at 6 months (risk difference 23 points, NNT 4), with dose reduction in a further 11%; the outcome was pharmacy refill records, not confirmed abstinence. D-PRESCRIBE sedative-hypnotic subgroup: 63/146 (43.2%) versus 14/155 (9.0%); 29 of 77 (38%) who tapered reported withdrawal symptoms. Both were Quebec community-pharmacy cluster trials.
scores.sharpen: Show the 27 versus 5 in 100 icon arrays, say that 62 in 100 recipients raised it with their doctor or pharmacist themselves, and close with what an older reader can ask their pharmacist for.

scores.accuracy_concern: The claim that time in bed grows after retirement, illness or a care home move has no source listed. Sleep restriction needs caution in people at high falls risk or who drive, and is unsuitable for some conditions. HABIT's mean age was 55, so cite Buysse (mean 71.7) for older adults.
scores.sharpen: Keep the clock question as the hook with a labelled illustrative time-in-bed bar, and make the teaching point the history question, not the trial, to stay distinct from C11-11.

scores.accuracy_concern: Morin 2004: n=76, mean age 62.5 (not an old-age sample), 10-week programme; 85%, 48% and 54% were drug-free after the initial intervention in the taper plus CBT, taper and CBT arms. 'No significant withdrawal symptoms' comes from a small trial, while D-PRESCRIBE found 38% of those tapering reported withdrawal symptoms; the two need reconciling in plain words.
scores.sharpen: Speak directly to the long-term user and say that sleep may take months to improve after stopping, so the ask is for a supervised plan with CBT, not willpower.

scores.accuracy_concern: Minor 2022 used wristband sleep-tracker data; its users are unlikely to represent poor or isolated older people. The 'lower-income' finding is about countries, not low-income individuals. The paper is not PubMed-indexed and UKHSA guidance was not openable, so the practical measures have no opened source.
scores.sharpen: Find an openable heat-health source for the bedroom measures or recast them as questions, and do not let the tracker data stand in for evidence about poor older people in hot flats.

scores.accuracy_concern: The intervention ran for five days, in four Los Angeles nursing homes; residents were 90% non-Hispanic white, and the trial dates from 2005. The only night-time effect was a small change in the length of awakenings (10.6 to 9.8 minutes versus 9.8 to 13.8 in controls), which should be described, not called a failure.
scores.sharpen: Open on the verdict-depends-on-the-measure point and show the 32 to 21 versus 32 to 30 bars, stating the five-day duration plainly on the chart.

scores.values_concern: Frame this as orders and routines set by the team, not as night staff waking patients carelessly.
scores.accuracy_concern: Wesselius 2018 covered adults aged 18 and over (median age 68) and asked about one night by self-report; 718 patients (35.8%) said staff woke them. SIESTA was one US centre, a before-after design with a comparison unit, not specific to older people; order changes rose on both units. The NEWS2 12-hourly minimum for a score of 0 needs an openable copy.
scores.sharpen: Make the ask a specific order written by the day team (protected sleep with observations clustered, unless clinically indicated) so night staff are backed rather than blamed.

scores.accuracy_concern: At 12 months, 67/119 (56.3%) versus 33/128 (25.8%) were in remission. The control group had education only, also by telephone, so the trial did not compare phone with digital CBT-I. All participants had osteoarthritis pain and belonged to one US health plan. The Ofcom internet-use figure was not openable.
scores.sharpen: Make the claim about access (a phone is enough, no internet needed) without implying phone beats apps, and name a UK route an older person could ask about.

scores.accuracy_concern: The SASM 2018 intraoperative guideline has not been read. The recommendation to continue CPAP around surgery is in the ASA 2014 and SASM 2016 guidance, which should be opened before citing. UK hospitals may require an electrical safety check of personal devices.
scores.sharpen: Add 'ask whether the ward needs to safety-check your machine' and cover emergency admissions, where a relative may need to bring the machine in.

scores.accuracy_concern: HABIT's mean age was 55.4 (range 19 to 88), so it is not an older-adult trial. ISI at 6 months was 10.9 versus 13.9. The AASM advice against sleep hygiene alone is a conditional recommendation.
scores.sharpen: Bring in Buysse 2011 (mean age 71.7, response 67% versus 25%) as the older-adult evidence and run this or C11-18, not both.

scores.accuracy_concern: In Glass 2005 the psychomotor adverse event result was reported as P>0.05, so 'unsteadiness more common' needs care. The zopiclone SPC and FDA zolpidem pages were not openable. The zolpidem dose change was a US regulatory action and should not be presented as UK advice.
scores.sharpen: Base the driving claim on an openable study of next-day driving impairment with zopiclone, and keep the timeline and three questions as the card.

scores.accuracy_concern: The participants were 38 adults aged 18 to 80 with mild to moderately severe hearing loss, tested in slow-wave sleep in a laboratory, so this is not an older-adult sample. What fire services offer varies by area. Check whether 520 Hz alarms are available in the UK before telling people to buy one.
scores.sharpen: Say plainly who was studied, add one concrete UK route (a fire and rescue home fire safety visit), and consider moving it to C14 if the sleep category is crowded.

scores.accuracy_concern: Ohayon 2004 pooled mostly small polysomnography samples published from 1960 to 2003. 'Most change has happened by 60' paraphrases 'only sleep efficiency continued to decrease after 60'. The NSF recommends 7 to 8 hours at 65 and over versus 7 to 9 for younger adults, so the saying is partly true and the post has to say so.
scores.sharpen: Test the saying fairly: somewhat lighter, more broken sleep is normal, a new change is a symptom, and then list the checkable causes.

scores.accuracy_concern: The ICS 2002 definition of nocturnal polyuria (more than a third of 24-hour urine at night in older people) needs the source opened. NICE CG97 and NG123 were not openable. The CPAP and nocturia meta-analysis pooled low-quality before-after studies.
scores.sharpen: Give the one-third rule with a filled, labelled illustrative chart a clinician can copy, and keep antimuscarinic harms to one line so it does not repeat E141.

scores.accuracy_concern: Glass 2005 pooled trials of at least five nights (short-term use) published 1966 to 2003. The 25.2 minutes is a subjective total sleep time. Do not turn the ORs (cognitive events 4.78, fatigue 3.82) into 'times more likely'. Psychomotor events were reported as P>0.05, so 'unsteadiness' needs care. Use NNT 13 and NNH 6 only after confirming them in the full text.
scores.sharpen: Set the 25 minutes against NNT and NNH icon arrays taken from the full text, and say the trials were short, so longer-term benefit is less certain.

scores.accuracy_concern: Sivertsen 2006: n=46, mean age 60.8. The placebo arm was followed only to 6 weeks, so the 6-month comparison is CBT versus zopiclone only.
scores.sharpen: Fold this into C11-16 or C11-11 as a supporting trial; on its own it gives the reader little reason to care now.

scores.accuracy_concern: Buysse 2011: n=79, primary outcome at 4 weeks (response 67% versus 25%, NNT 2.4), maintained at 6 months. HABIT's mean age was 55, so it does not show effect in older adults.
scores.sharpen: If kept, make it the older-adult service-model post (who can deliver it and how short it is) and drop HABIT; otherwise merge Buysse into C11-11.

scores.accuracy_concern: The claim that daytime sleepiness in later life comes from illness, medicines and sleep disorders rather than age has no checked source (the leads are 'unsure'). The BNF was not openable for the drug list. The Glass fatigue finding covers hypnotics only.
scores.sharpen: Find one checked epidemiological source on causes of daytime sleepiness in older people and add that sleepiness which is new or getting worse is a reason to see the GP soon.

scores.accuracy_concern: Polysomnography finds very high rates of apnoea in older people (HypnoLaus), much of it of uncertain clinical significance, so 'consider OSA even without sleepiness' risks overdiagnosis. The claim that older people report less sleepiness rests on a review marked 'unsure'. NICE NG202 was not openable.
scores.sharpen: Balance the prompt with evidence on who benefits from CPAP in later life (for example the PREDICT trial) so the post does not push testing for everyone who snores.

scores.accuracy_concern: Postuma 2019 drew on 24 specialist sleep centres: polysomnography-confirmed idiopathic RBD, 82.5% men, mean age 66. Conversion covers Parkinson's disease, DLB and MSA. Dream enactment reported in the community will predict less. Sleep apnoea can mimic RBD.
scores.sharpen: Keep the Ask, Assess, Protect, Talk card and say that the 73.5% at 12 years comes from specialist-centre patients, so it is not a personal prognosis for everyone who acts out dreams.

scores.accuracy_concern: The AASM 2025 iron thresholds (ferritin 75 ng/mL or lower, or transferrin saturation below 20%) are consensus that has 'not been empirically tested'. The guideline also conditionally suggests opioids. It is a US guideline, and NICE CKS may still list dopamine agonists, so say where UK practice differs.
scores.sharpen: Open on the surprising point that a ferritin reported as normal can still be low for restless legs, and label it clearly as a 2025 US guideline.

scores.accuracy_concern: Billioti de Gage 2014: adjusted OR 1.51 (1.43 after adjusting for anxiety, depression and insomnia). Gray 2016: HR 1.07 (0.82 to 1.39) at the highest use, and the most recent year of use was excluded to limit reverse causation. Several meta-analyses of observational studies report a pooled association; leaving them out would look like choosing two studies to fit.
scores.sharpen: Say that pooled observational studies show an association, explain reverse causation in one plain sentence, and keep the do-not-stop-suddenly instruction.

scores.accuracy_concern: Cochrane 2020 found low-certainty evidence that melatonin up to 10 mg may have little or no effect in Alzheimer's disease (total night sleep MD 10.7 min, CI crossing zero); the same review found some benefit for trazodone and orexin antagonists, so do not imply nothing helps. Melatonin is prescription-only in the UK, so the content-variability studies describe North American supplements. The Circadin SPC was not openable.
scores.sharpen: Add that melatonin is prescription-only in the UK, so products bought online are unregulated, and give the reader a review-date question.

scores.values_concern: Avoid implying blame of prescribers as a group; many such prescriptions start in hospital or specialist care in good faith.
scores.accuracy_concern: The stroke and death warnings apply to people with dementia; extending them to all older people needs its own source. Harms of low-dose quetiapine need a specific checked cohort study (the lead is 'unsure').
scores.sharpen: Keep the statement card, add a practical review step (record the reason, agree a slow taper), and cite a checked source on harms at low dose.

scores.accuracy_concern: McCurry 2007's 'two-thirds' figure is a background estimate in a review, not a study finding. The link between night-time disturbance and care home admission needs a primary cohort (Hope 1998 is marked unsure). Carer assessment law differs across the UK nations.
scores.sharpen: Replace the two-thirds figure with a primary study of carer sleep, and give the carer the exact sentence to use in the assessment.

scores.values_concern: Night checks can be needed for safety; word the questions so they invite the home to explain rather than accusing care workers.
scores.accuracy_concern: Alessi's 339 of 492 is a US screening sample, not a prevalence figure for UK homes. The Schnelle 1993 and 1999 leads are unverified. CQC Regulation 9 applies in England only.
scores.sharpen: Cut to four questions with the best evidence (bedtimes, night checks, continence care, noise and light) and cite the care standard for each UK nation.

scores.accuracy_concern: Irwin 2022: 12.2% versus 25.9% (HR 0.51). The protocol was amended to extend follow-up from 24 to 36 months, and only 52% to 57% completed 36 months. At 24 months completion was 73% (CBT-I) versus 87% (sleep education). Single site, 83% White, and people with a major health event in the past year were excluded.
scores.sharpen: Show the 12 versus 26 in 100 icon arrays over 'up to three years', and name the uneven drop-out in the limitation strip.

scores.accuracy_concern: Fralick 2019: 146 versus 11 per 1,000 person-years (HR 13.2) for the older desmopressin formulation, in a US commercial insurance database. The outcome was a coded hyponatraemia diagnosis, and only 20% had a baseline sodium. The newer low-dose formulations were not studied.
scores.sharpen: Say the data are for the older formulation, and add the practical monitoring rule (baseline sodium, early recheck) from an openable source.

scores.accuracy_concern: The Ebrahim 2013 review draws largely on young healthy volunteers. The claim about age and blood alcohol has no source. Stopping suddenly is unsafe for people who drink heavily every day.
scores.sharpen: Add one sentence that anyone who drinks heavily every day should get advice before stopping, and find a checked source on older people and alcohol.

scores.accuracy_concern: McDowell 1998 compared a pre-intervention rate of 51/94 (54%) with 34/111 (31%) in a different cohort on one ward in the 1990s. Chronic users refused the protocol more often (64% versus 41%) and still received hypnotics more often. Back rubs and relaxation tapes are dated.
scores.sharpen: Update the routine for today's wards (a warm caffeine-free drink, relaxation audio, offered before any tablet) and state the before-after caveat plainly.

allocation_reason: 30 of 31 candidates clear the ~36 bar (only C11-19 is near it at 37; note that the stated formula's true maximum is 55, not 50) and about 18 distinct candidates score 44.5 or more with no disqualifying flag, so sleep supports the maximum; fill it by taking one from each overlapping pair (C11-11 or C11-18; C11-15 or C11-29) and no more than three or four sleeping-tablet posts.
balance_note: The top 14 by score are practitioner-heavy: 6 practitioner (C11-21, C11-11, C11-22, C11-02, C11-29, C11-15), 5 both (C11-16, C11-03, C11-23, C11-28, C11-07) and only 3 public (C11-13, C11-10, C11-24). To keep substantial public coverage, swap one of the nocturia pair and C11-25 or C11-08 for public candidates C11-27 (care home nights), C11-05 (stopping after years) or C11-26 (carer's nights). No 'Who gets left out' post is in the top 14, so C11-09 or C11-26 would add that series. The sleeping-tablet cluster (C11-16, C11-03, C11-23, then C11-25, C11-05, C11-12) should be capped at three or four.
notes: Scored blind from /tmp/blind_C11.json. Key figures for C11-03, 05, 07, 08, 09, 11, 13, 14, 16, 18, 21, 22, 23, 24, 28, 29 and 31 were checked against PubMed abstracts during scoring. Accuracy notes flag where abstracts differ from or qualify the candidate text: the McCurry two-thirds figure is a background estimate; Glass reported psychomotor events as P>0.05; HABIT's mean age was 55; Irwin's 36-month follow-up was incomplete. No candidate is delirium-topic and none substantially repeats an earlier post. C11-13 may fit C14 (hearing) better than C11.
